# Laboratory Safety and Emergencies
Corporate Security has authority during an emergency, and its instructions override this handbook.
## Laboratory Safety - Lab coat, gloves and eye protection must be worn when handling chemicals or samples. - Staff must know where the nearest emergency shower and medical kit are. - Unknown substances may not be tasted, smelled or touched. - Spills are to be cleaned straight away. If the substance is unknown, staff are to leave the room, close the door and report it to the Lead Researcher. - Every injury, however small, must be reported and seen by medical staff.
## Containment Breach If a specimen escapes, or staff suspect it has: - Staff must leave the laboratory immediately. They may not try to recapture the specimen or stop for their work. - Staff are to close and lock the doors behind them if it is safe to do so. - The breach must be reported on the Company radio channel: what escaped, where it was last seen, and whether anyone is hurt. - Staff must wait somewhere secure until Security gives the all-clear, and may not go back in. - A breach may not be discussed on any open channel, and colonial staff may not be told what escaped. Security will warn colonists if they are at risk.
## Exposure - Suspected exposure to specimen blood, venom, spores or tissue must be reported at once. - Exposed staff are to go to medical staff without waiting for symptoms, and tell them it is a laboratory exposure. The Company will handle the rest.
## Hostile Intrusion The procedure in the Employee Handbook applies: leave if it is safe, lock yourself in if it isn't, report it on the Company radio channel, and wait for the all-clear. If there is time before leaving, staff should lock away samples and sensitive data, but not at any risk to themselves.
## Evacuation - Staff are to go where Security directs and stay with the group. - Research staff and their data have priority for any Company shuttle. Staff must be at the landing zone on time.
## After an Incident - Staff must give the Lead Researcher a written account while it is fresh. - Incidents may not be discussed with anyone else.
